subject: Clarifying CCPA/CPRA forwarding exemptions and subprocessor onboarding orchestration
messages:
From: Elena Morales <emorales@blueharborhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Trevor Mills <trevor.mills@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification needed: CCPA forwarding exemptions & subprocessor onboarding orchestration

Hi Michael —

Thanks for taking this. Our privacy team is reviewing the DPA appendix and we hit a couple of places where we need clarification so we can sign off with procurement:

1) Forwarding/"sale" exemptions under CCPA/CPRA: can you confirm whether any customer data (telemetry, logs, aggregated metrics) is ever forwarded to third parties for purposes outside of providing the service (analytics vendors, ad/CDN partners)? If so, who are those third parties, and on what contractual basis do you rely on an exception (service provider vs sale exemption)?

2) Subprocessor onboarding/orchestration: what's Redwood's typical notice period when you add a new subprocessor, and do you offer an emergency onboarding flow (for incidents) with an SLA? We need both the regular notice window and any emergency clause text.

3) Evidence: for a sample audit, what docs can you provide for subprocessor vetting (SOC2, encryption attestations, subprocessors list)?

We're trying to lock timelines — procurement needs to know whether a standard 30-day notice works, or if you require more negotiation. Attached is a short checklist from our side (not exhaustive).

Thanks —
Elena Morales
Senior Counsel, Privacy
BlueHarbor Health
[Attachment: bh_privacy_checklist_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <emorales@blueharborhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification needed: CCPA forwarding exemptions & subprocessor onboarding orchestration

Elena —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers below and attaching our current subprocessor list (v1) for your review. Priyom/ Iren e, please jump in for legal framing.

Summary answers (high-level):
- Classification: Redwood operates as a service provider under CPRA/CCPA for hosted inference — we do not "sell" customer personal information. We process customer data to provide inference and observability; contractual limits prevent resale.
- Forwarding: We forward small telemetry/usage aggregates to a handful of vendors (CDN for model artifact distribution; analytics provider for anonymized usage metrics). Those vendors are under contract as subprocessors and do not use the data for their independent commercial purposes. No advertising companies are receiving customer PII.
- Notice: Standard practice is 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; emergency onboarding is available for security/incident response with an expedited notification and post-facto approval in exceptional cases.
- Evidence: We can provide a SOC 2 report for the service, our subprocessors list (attached), and standard encryption attestations (TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest).

Attachments: subprocessors_list_v1.pdf (contains names + high-level functions).

Next steps: Irene, can you confirm whether the language below is sufficient for the DPA (I pasted the suggested clause after my signature)? Elena — if that looks OK we'll prepare a short addendum with the explicit 30-day notice plus a defined emergency onboarding workflow.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

---- Suggested DPA snippets (draft, legal to confirm) ----
1) Service provider classification: "Vendor shall act solely as a service provider as defined under the California Consumer Privacy Act and the California Privacy Rights Act. Vendor will not sell, share, or monetize Customer Personal Information except to the extent necessary to perform the services set forth in the Agreement and subject to contractual restrictions on onward use by subprocessors."

2) Subprocessor notice: "Vendor will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of the addition of any new subprocessor and will provide a reasonably detailed description of the processing activities and security controls. In emergency circumstances (security incident or regulatory requirement), Vendor may onboard a subprocessor on an expedited basis provided that Vendor notifies Customer as soon as practicable and provides subsequent documentation and remediation rights consistent with the Agreement."

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <emorales@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification needed: CCPA forwarding exemptions & subprocessor onboarding orchestration

Michael / Priyom —

Thanks for drafting. A few legal edits and clarifications before we send anything final to BlueHarbor:

- Service provider wording: prefer to reference the specific statutory language to avoid ambiguity. Suggest: "Vendor acts as a Service Provider under the CCPA and a Processor under any applicable state privacy law, and will not engage in selling, sharing, or targeted advertising using Customer Personal Information except as expressly permitted by Customer in writing."

- Forwarding: clarify telemetry categories ("aggregated telemetry", "model artifact distribution", "support logs") and confirm that any forwarded telemetry is pseudonymized and cannot be re-identified by the recipient. If BlueHarbor requires, we can add a carve-out listing the limited categories that may be forwarded.

- Notice periods: 30 days' prior notice is standard; for emergency onboarding we should include a firm max-post-notice window and a remediation/rollback right. Proposed language: "Emergency onboarding: Vendor may onboard a subprocessor within five (5) business days in response to a bona fide security incident or urgent operational need, provided Vendor notifies Customer within one (1) business day and provides written justification and a remediation plan; Customer retains the right to require termination of the subprocessor if Vendor fails to remediate within thirty (30) days."

- Security proof: we can provide SOC 2 Type II (redacted) and an attestation of encryption-in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and encryption-at-rest (AES-256). For subprocessors we can provide the most recent third-party attestations where available; some smaller vendors have self-attestations which we'll flag.

I attached a short snippet for the DPA with the emergency onboarding wording. Happy to send this as an addendum draft to BlueHarbor after Michael signs off on tone.

-Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ccpa_role_snippet.docx (docx)]

Subject: Re: Clarification needed: CCPA forwarding exemptions & subprocessor onboarding orchestration

Michael / Irene / Priyom —

Thanks — this is helpful and much clearer. A couple of quick operational asks before procurement will push the DocuSign:

- BlueHarbor can accept the service provider/processor framing provided the telemetry categories are limited and the recipients are listed in an appendix. Please include the CDN + analytics provider names in the subprocessors appendix (we saw the attached list, but the appendix in the DPA needs explicit names).
- Notice: 30 days is acceptable for routine additions. For emergency onboarding we can agree to your proposed 5 business day window provided Redwood commits to the 1 business day notification and the 30-day remediation/termination right.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II redacted and an encryption attestation are sufficient initially; procurement may request deeper evidence for any subprocessor that handles unredacted logs.

If you can prepare a short DocuSign-ready addendum with the updated appendix and the emergency onboarding clause, Trevor (cc'd) will route through procurement. Suggested timeline: 2 weeks for legal + procurement to review once the addendum is shared.

Best —
Elena Morales
Senior Counsel, Privacy
BlueHarbor Health
